text_devanagari: ए॒वा ह॑स्य॒ काम्या॒ स्तोम॑ उ॒क्थं च॒ शंस्या॑ । इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ ६ ॥
y_bands: Measured on the leaf text block (3216x4826 px; the block origin is the global line-x origin). Line 5 ink runs y997-1112 and the line pitch is ~174 px. Full-width row-ink profile gives, top to bottom: LINE-ABOVE (line 4) ANUDATTA BAR BAND y962-975 (line 4's own bars, 36-39 px wide, 11-12 px tall); BLANK GUTTER y976-994 (exactly zero inked pixels across all 3216 columns) - this is what separates the two bar layers; MY SVARITA / ABOVE-HEADLINE BAND y993-1026 (every mark standing clear of my headline, none touching it); MY SIROREKHA y1029-1045 (peak 2310 inked px in row y1041); MY GLYPH BODIES y1046-1110; MY DESCENDER BAND y1105-1127 (u/uu matra tails, the swash tails of the initial vowels, the numeral tail), all continuous with the bodies; BLANK y1128-1131; MY OWN ANUDATTA BAR BAND y1132-1148, mark cores y1134-1146; then zero ink from y1149 to y1344, and line 6's above-headline band opens at y1345 (line 6 sirorekha ~y1378). My bar band sits 172 px below the line-above bar band, one full line pitch, and 89-104 px below my own sirorekha; line 4's bar band sits at the same 104-117 px offset below line 4's sirorekha (y857), which confirms the attribution.
boundary_interpretation: Word boundaries come from breaks in the sirorekha, read as connected components of the row band y1029-1045: inside a word the headline is unbroken; it stops only at a word space. Headline groups measured in global line-x: 341-534, 575-783, 822-1110, 1149-1383, 1422-1661, 1698-1787, 1828-2065, [2107-2123 = single danda, no headline], 2166-2437, 2472-2922, [2984-2999 and 3007-3023 = double danda, 3052-3097 = numeral, 3143-3180 = double danda, no headline]. Word gaps are 37-52 px wide and cut the headline; aksara boundaries inside a word appear only in the body band (y1046-1110) as 6-22 px white columns with the headline running on above them, so the two kinds of gap are never confusable. Aksara boundaries used (global line-x): word0 e|vaa ~419; word1 ha|sya ~666; word2 kaa|myaa ~949; word3 stoo|ma ~1298; word4 u|kthaM ~1502; word6 shaM|syaa ~1904; word7 i|ndraa ~2230 and ndraa|ya ~2356; word8 soo|ma ~2591, ma|pii ~2673, pii|ta ~2780, ta|ye ~2850. Marks that sit near a boundary, and how each was assigned: (a) svarita x647 in word 1 - its full extent is 640-657 even at the loosest threshold, entirely left of the ha|sya body gap at 663-669, and it stands directly on that aksara's own stem (642-660); assigned to the first aksara, not to sya. (b) anudatta x1479 in ukthaM - the tightest case on the line: the bar runs 1459-1500 and its right edge just reaches the right edge of u, but its centre is 23 px left of the u|kthaM gap (1493-1511) and the whole bar lies under the belly of u; assigned to u. (c) svarita x2304 in indraaya - 68 px right of i|ndraa and 47 px left of ndraa|ya, with body ink of the dra cluster directly beneath it (x2277-2313 at y1089-1104); assigned to ndraa. (d) svarita x2652 in somapiitaye - only 21 px left of the ma|pii boundary, but it stands exactly on ma's own stem (2648-2663) and 61 px from the soo|ma boundary; assigned to ma, not pii. (e) anudatta x2407 - extent 2389-2426, wholly inside ya (2358-2437), 33 px right of ndraa|ya; assigned to ya. (f) anudatta x362 - extent 344-380, wholly inside the first aksara (341-425), 39 px left of the e|vaa gap at 408-429. (g) anudatta x1040 in kaamyaa - extent 1021-1059, 72 px right of the kaa|myaa gap (938-959) and directly under the ya stem of the myaa cluster; assigned to myaa. (h) anudatta x1759 - under the one-aksara word ca (body 1699-1780), with 41 px of clear paper to shaMsyaa on the right and 79 px to ukthaM on the left; no alternative carrier. No mark on this line straddles a word gap.
notes: MAGNIFICATION. I started from the two supplied 1568 px segment crops, then rendered my own crops of the same line straight from the leaf JPEG at 2.3x, 2.5x, 2.9x, 4.7x, 5.4x and 7.3x of leaf-block scale, plus binarised versions. The leaf is a 4000 px upscale of a 2024 px master, so a leaf-block pixel is about half a real scan pixel and nothing past ~2.5x adds information; the extra magnification was only for spatial judgement. The decisive evidence is measurement, not viewing: full-width row-ink profiles, per-band 8-connected component extents, and step-1/2/3 ASCII ink maps computed with PIL at thresholds 85, 100, 110, 128, 135, 150 and 170. STABILITY. All eleven marks are present at every threshold from 110 to 170 and no twelfth candidate appears. At thr128 the six bars measure 37, 38, 39, 37, 38, 38 px wide and 11, 11, 12, 11, 10, 10 px tall; the five upright strokes measure 12, 12, 11, 11 and 13 px wide and 32, 32, 31, 31, 31 px tall. Both sets sit squarely inside the shapes the brief describes, and no bar is taller than wide nor any stroke wider than tall. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES. (1) Ten bars in the y962-975 band, at x362, 759, 989, 1029, 1255, 1609, 2110, 2312, 2672 and 2789. These are line 4's own anudatta bars: one full line pitch (172 px) above my bar band and cut off from my line by the completely blank gutter y976-994. The ones at x2110 and x2312 are the traps - x2110 sits directly above my danda and x2312 directly above indraaya, so at band scale they read as marks on my line. Note also x362, which sits at the same x as one of MY bars, one band up. (2) Four wide curved matras above my headline: x1213-1284 (o of stoo), x2507-2579 (o of soo), x2709-2770 (ii of pii), x2850-2912 (e of ye) - 62 to 73 px across, four to six times too wide for a 6-16 px upright stroke. (3) Two round dots, x1627-1651 (25x28 px) and x1880-1902 (23x23 px): aspect ratio 1.0-1.1, as wide as tall, so anusvara over kthaM and over shaM, not svarita. (4) x3057-3097 above headline level by the verse numeral, 41x22 px: continuous with the numeral body, which runs y1005-1125, so it is the top of the digit, not a free-standing mark. (5) A 59x2 px sliver at x1504-1562, y1025-1026 - the extreme top of the ktha ligature clipped by my band edge. (6) Two flecks: 6x3 px at x2078-2083 y1023-1025 just left of the danda, and 4x3 px at x359-362 y1153-1155 just below my first bar; both under 12 inked pixels, an order of magnitude below any accent. (7) Descenders reaching y1105-1127 at x2214-2245 and x2275-2323 (the i and dra tails of indraaya), x3071-3110 (numeral tail), and the swash tail of word 0's first aksara at x390-416: every one is continuous with its own glyph body with no white gap, so none is a bar. UNRESOLVED 1 of 2. Word 0, aksara 0. The ink is a downward wedge of two short strokes hanging from the headline with a teardrop counter between them (white at x374-388, y1046-1066), merging low into a swash tail that runs down-right to y1112; it has no plain full-height stem reaching the baseline. I read it as e. Reasons: this fount gives its independent vowels swash tails - the i of indraaya does the same, tailing to y1122 - while ordinary consonant stems on this line are plain verticals; and my own unprompted reading of the glyph at low magnification was e, not vocalic-r or shra, which is the misreading the brief's fount note says a provokes. I still record it as unclear, because on silhouette alone a cannot be excluded and the fount note may be aimed at exactly this glyph. The accent is unaffected either way: the bar at x362 belongs to this aksara. UNRESOLVED 2 of 2. Word 1, aksara 0. The ink shows a single consonant here, not a conjunct. Its body is 79 px wide (x582-660), the same as the single consonant ca (x1699-1780, 82 px), whereas every consonant-plus-ya conjunct on this line is 114-120 px wide (sya at x670-783 is 114 px; the m+ya of kaamyaa is 120 px), because this fount always writes ya with its own crescent counter and its own stem. This glyph has no ya element, and there is no ink at all below y1112 beneath it, so there is no stacked subscript either. On shape - upper-left curve, lower-left loop, a hook descending down-right, and a plain right stem at x642-660 - I read ha, giving hasya. I record it unclear because a reader who knows the corpus will expect hyasya here and I cannot formally exclude an unusually narrow hya ligature; but the width evidence is against it and, per the brief, I have followed the ink rather than the expectation. The accent is unaffected: svarita on this aksara, anudatta on sya. The verse numeral I read as 6 - a top hook, an S-curve, a lower-right loop and a descending tail, y1005-1125; 5, 8 and 9 do not fit the silhouette, but I hold this at moderate confidence only, and it is not an aksara so it is not counted in unclear_count. All coordinates here are leaf-text-block x, which is the brief's global line-x (block width 3216); I measured the source image directly rather than converting from the rendered crops, so no 0.9469 rescale was applied.
